Ordinary C++17, OpenMP and x86 intrinsics are available. Do not modify the protected correctness or timing protocol. Scratch allocation inside run is allowed and included in timing. The optimized reference source is withheld. Choose topics independently, record failed attempts, complete memory integration and independently confirm final G.

model_interpretation.claim: Earlier T1 lane-state variants were correct and measured about 0.990 µs, while the sentinel/masked-tail variant measured about 1.718 µs; the baseline measured about 4.463 µs. This candidate contrasts with a single dependent lane-state stream by interleaving two independent AVX-512 state banks and processing full vectors in pairs. It may shorten dependency chains and reduce loop overhead, but the extra state and final reduction may offset that benefit. No speedup is assumed; compare correctness and repeated timings under the frozen one-thread protocol.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.cpp"],"retained":["Maintain two independent AVX-512 banks of signed lane minima and earliest absolute indices. Seed the first bank with vector zero and the second with vector one when available; process later complete vectors in pairs across the banks.","Update each bank only on a strict signed improvement, retaining its earlier index on ties. Combine both banks by value then index; a sentinel second bank cannot beat any valid input index, including when values equal INT32_MAX.","Use a scalar path for n below 16 and a scalar tuple-ordered tail after all complete vectors, preserving index zero for non-positive n and handling INT32_MIN, INT32_MAX, and equal minima."]}

model_interpretation.claim: The catalog's single-accumulator first pass with a four-vector equality search measured 4.3046e-7 seconds, while four-accumulator variants paired with one- or eight-vector searches measured 5.2660e-7 and 4.5678e-7 seconds. Those results do not isolate the interaction. This candidate pairs four independent minimum accumulators with the four-vector search to test whether reducing first-pass dependency chains helps without losing the search loop's observed benefit. It preserves signed comparisons, earliest-match order, and tail handling; random and decreasing inputs may still differ in second-pass work.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.cpp"],"retained":["Change the first-pass minimum reduction to four independent AVX-512F accumulators over groups of four vectors, then combine accumulators and process remaining vectors and scalar tail.","Unroll the second-pass equality search across four vectors; examine vector masks in index order and use the lowest set lane to preserve earliest-index ties.","Retain bounds-safe vector remainder and scalar-tail paths, including nonpositive sizes and INT32 extrema."]}

model_interpretation.claim: A six-way scalar unroll tests whether a moderate number of independent minimum/index chains can approach the measured two- and eight-accumulator results while avoiding the overhead that may have hurt three and four accumulators. It may help most on decreasing inputs, where each lane's minimum is repeatedly updated; on random inputs, extra comparisons and the final fold may outweigh reduced loop-carried dependence. Prior measurements are aggregate, so per-pattern outcomes remain to be checked after correctness validation.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/candidate.cpp"],"retained":["Replaced the single-chain scan with a fixed six-way scalar scan using six independent minimum-value and index accumulators.","Folded the six results using signed minimum-value comparison and lowest-index tie-breaking.","Handled inputs smaller than six with a scalar scan and processed any remaining elements scalarly after the fold.","Used no explicit SIMD and no parallel workers."]}

Réduire les minima de lane avec la réduction vectorielle signée, puis choisir le plus petit indice parmi les lanes égales au minimum.
Traiter les tailles inférieures à 16 et le reste scalaire sans perdre la règle du premier indice en cas d’égalité.

experiments.hypothesis: Le suivi des minima signés et de leur premier indice par lane peut supprimer le second balayage d’égalité de T2. Le coût des masques et des mises à jour d’indices peut toutefois annuler ce gain; seule la mesure comparable au T2 décidera.

research_assignment.objective: Partir de T2/8d, la candidate mesurée la plus rapide, et intégrer le suivi intercalé de deux états lane de T1/9ac pour supprimer le second balayage. Tester une réduction vectorielle finale des minima et l’extraction tie-aware du plus petit indice, au lieu du repli scalaire coûteux. Préserver les queues et toute la sémantique de correction; mesurer sans supposer un gain.
research_assignment.stop_condition: Si la correction échoue ou si l’intégration ne bat pas T2/8d dans une comparaison mesurée comparable, conserver T2/8d et arrêter les intégrations supplémentaires; procéder à la sélection finale et à la confirmation indépendante.
research_assignment.subject: T2 avec états lane intercalés et réduction vectorielle finale de T1

retained: Remplacer le second balayage de recherche par deux banques indépendantes de minima signés et d’indices, mises à jour strictement pour conserver les occurrences les plus précoces dans chaque voie.
Réduire vectoriellement les minima combinés, puis masquer les indices qui n’égalent pas le minimum et réduire les indices restants pour appliquer la règle du plus petit indice.
Conserver le chemin scalaire pour n < 16, les vecteurs complets, le vecteur complet isolé éventuel et la queue scalaire; rendre best_value mutable afin que cette queue compile.

experiments.hypothesis: Les deux banques de minima lane intercalées évitent le second balayage de T2 et réduisent la dépendance sérielle; réduire en SIMD les minima puis les indices à égalité peut aussi éviter le repli scalaire final. Le coût des comparaisons, masques et réductions pourrait annuler ces bénéfices, donc aucun gain n’est présumé. Cette réparation rend compilable l’intégration après le diagnostic de l’assignation à best_value const.

Retaining the ordered four-vector equality search preserves earliest-index selection. The interaction and performance still require measurement.
